description:
'''Twee pop''' is a [[subgenre]] of [[indie pop]] that originally emerged in the United Kingdom during the mid-to-late 1980s. The style has been described as "excessively or affectedly quaint, pretty, or sentimental" and initially rose to prominence through the ''[[NME]]'s'' ''[[C86]]'' cassette compilation, with ''[[AllMusic]]'' describing twee as "simplicity and innocence" as well as "boy-girl [[Harmony|harmonies]], lovelorn lyrics, infectious [[Melody|melodies]], and simple, unaffected performances." 

The scene was originally spearheaded by [[Sarah Records]] in the United Kingdom, which housed acts such as [[The Field Mice]], [[Heavenly (British band)|Heavenly]], and [[The Orchids]], along with [[Calvin Johnson (musician)|Calvin Johnson]] of [[Beat Happening]]'s [[K Records]] in the United States. The genre continued to develop throughout the 1990s and 2000s. During the late 2000s and early to mid-2010s, a broader twee aesthetic gained prominence in popular culture, becoming associated with indie music, vintage-inspired fashion, and films, while finding a substantial following on social media platforms such as [[Tumblr]]. In the early 2020s, the aesthetic experienced renewed interest amongst [[Generation Z]] through [[TikTok]], particularly as part of a broader revival of early 2010s fashion and internet culture. This revival inspired a microgenre known as "[[laptop twee]]."
